# Companion system

Atelier's companion is assembled at runtime from modular parts. The pieces are:
- 3D parts for each slot;
- a 2D expression layer drawn onto a UV-mapped face surface;
- JSON rules for which parts fit together, hat placement, pupil movement and randomization;
- a few base rigs with animation clips and timed animation events;
- off-screen rendering for the Dock icon;
- preset companions, and an editor.

**All art is generated by code** in `scripts/companion-assets/`.

The shared contract (ids, types, file formats) is `src/shared/companion.ts`. This document describes the conventions the generator, the runtime and the integration code share.

## Licensing

The engine is open source under the [MPL-2.0](../LICENSE): the contract (`src/shared/companion.ts`), the look rules (`src/shared/companionLogic.ts`), the runtime (`src/renderer/src/companion/`), the kit (`src/kit/`) and main's side (`src/main/companion.ts`, `src/main/companions.ts`). The art is not: the generated files in `src/renderer/public/companion/`, their recipes in `scripts/companion-assets/`, and the six Atelier characters (Pip, Juniper, Bolt, Mochi, Sage and Pepper) are Atelier Companion Art, under the [Atelier Companion Art License](../ART-LICENSE.md). Anyone may make characters from it for Atelier and share them, in `.ateliercompanion` files, packs, apps and worlds too, and a character of your own may be your brand's mascot inside Atelier. Builds made from this repository, with or without changes, may include the art when they are shared so others can test or review changes for Atelier (pull-request previews, testers, CI artifacts; section 2.1). The art can't be used outside Atelier, and a build you distribute as your own product (a fork) uses a name and icons of its own and its own character designs in place of the art (section 3.1; see [Bring your own designs](#bring-your-own-designs)). The six characters are trademarks ([TRADEMARKS.md](../TRADEMARKS.md)). Each art folder has a `LICENSE.md`, and the art's source files carry the art notice instead of the MPL one.

No character is written into the engine. `DEFAULT_LOOK` is the branding's default companion's look (Pip's comes from `presets.json` in official builds), or `PLAIN_LOOK`, the unofficial branding's neutral companion, in code bundled without the branding.

## Files

```
scripts/companion-assets/        generator (Node, ESM .mjs): geometry, animation, SVG, config, compression
src/renderer/public/companion/   generated output, committed; served at app://atelier/companion/
  manifest.json                  CompanionManifest
  rigs/A.glb B.glb C.glb         base rigs with animation clips
  parts/<part-id>.glb            one file per 3D part
  face/<face-id>/<variant>.svg   2D face layers; eyes also have pupils.svg
  config/head-part-compatibility.json
  config/hat-config.json
  config/eye-pupil-config.json
  config/randomization-config.json
  config/animation-events.json
  config/presets.json
```

`npm run companion:assets` regenerates everything deterministically (no randomness without a fixed seed, and no timestamps), so the output only changes when the generator does.

## 3D conventions

- **Axes and units:** +Y up, +Z toward the camera, 1 unit ≈ the height of rig A's body. The root sits on the ground (y = 0) with feet at y ≈ 0.
- **Rig `.glb`:** node hierarchy `root › body › head-pivot › anchor:head`, plus `body › arm.L`, `body › arm.R › anchor:prop`, and `root › foot.L`, `root › foot.R`. Body, arm and foot meshes are children of those nodes.
- **Rig sizes:** rig A is round and roughly as wide as it is tall; rig B is taller and slimmer; rig C is small and stubby with a larger head scale.
- **Rig animations** are glTF animations named exactly as `CLIPS` (`idle listen think work talk alert celebrate sad sleep wave poke`).
  - They animate only TRS of `RIG_NODES`.
  - Looping clips last 2–4 s and are seamless (first key equals last).
  - `wave` and `poke` are one-shots of about 1–1.5 s.
- **Walk and run** aren't in the rig files: `locomotion.ts` poses them in code on the nodes every rig has (feet, arms, body, head pivot), once per rig from its rest pose, over the same 21 channels as the rig's own clips (the walk the website's sprite sheets pose). `Animator.setMoving('walk' | 'run' | null, { rate })` plays one in the mood clip's place while the face keeps the mood; `gaitRate` matches the steps to the ground speed. Worlds and the kit's `move()` use them; pages that show stills (the new tab floor) get a strip of eight frames from `renderCompanionWalk`, drawn once per look in idle time and stepped by CSS on the compositor.
- **Head part:** a node named by its id, built around the anchor origin (the neck point), containing:
  - head meshes using `tint:skin`;
  - a mesh named `face`: a UV-mapped surface just outside the head front (u from 0 to 1 left to right, v from 0 to 1 bottom to top), with a material named `face`, which the runtime replaces with the face texture;
  - empty nodes `anchor:hat`, `anchor:hair`, `anchor:ears`, `anchor:eyeAccessory`, `anchor:earAccessory`, placed for that head's shape.
- **Other parts:** one node named by the id, modelled relative to its anchor's origin.
- **Materials:**
  - `tint:<skin|hair|accent|outfit>` are recoloured from the profile;
  - `paint:<name>` keep their base colour (white, ink, gold and so on);
  - flat base colours only, no textures; the runtime applies the toon look.
- **Fitting:** a fit pass in the generator measures every head and writes the configs from the geometry:
  - `head-part-compatibility.json` has one entry per head (the hair that covers it, and so on) and one per hat that restricts what goes with it: hair that would poke through, and ears that would clip through or vanish inside it. A look wearing the hat must satisfy both; when they clash, the hat wins.
  - `hat-config.json` seats every part worn over the head (each hat, plus headphones) on every head. Hair raises the seat, so a head entry can carry `hair` replacements, one per hair style that moves the part. Rings (crowns, beret) are lifted onto the hair, shells (beanie, cap) grow until head and hair are covered, and the headphone band grows until it clears both. Shells only grow over a hair style's covering cap, so the generator also checks every hair a shell hat accepts along the hat's front edge, where its brim or cuff sits: a lock or fringe that would cut through them stops generation until the hair is listed as a conflict.
- **Optimization:** run through glTF-Transform (dedup, weld, prune, quantize, `EXT_meshopt_compression`). Aim for under 60 KB per part and under 150 KB per rig. Keep triangle counts modest: under 4.5k per head and per part (the asset test enforces both). Most accessories land between 1.5k and 3k; the curls, beanie, beret and wizard hat are the heaviest at about 4k. A fully dressed companion is about 25k triangles before the outline hull doubles them.

## Face layer conventions

- Every SVG has a 512×256 viewBox and a transparent background. Ink colour is `#1d1630`, highlights `#ffffff`, and the mouth interior `#4a1f3a`.
- **Layout:**
  - eye centres at (176, 112) and (336, 112);
  - brows around y = 60 above each eye;
  - mouth centre at (256, 190).
  - Eyes and brows are mirrored left and right inside the one layer.
- **Variants:** every face id provides every variant in its list (`EYE_VARIANTS`, `BROW_VARIANTS`, `MOUTH_VARIANTS`). Missing variants are a generator bug.
- **Pupils:** for eyes, `pupils.svg` holds both pupils with their highlights. The runtime offsets it by `gaze × range` from `eye-pupil-config.json`, and shows it only for the variants listed in `pupilVariants`. Eye-white shapes go in the variant file; pupils never do. Pupils are not clipped to the whites, so at every gaze the runtime shows a variant with, the pupil may cover the white's outline but never reach the skin; the asset test checks this geometrically.

## Runtime (renderer)

`src/renderer/src/companion/index.ts` exports:

```ts
Companion            // React component: { profile: CompanionProfile; mood: CompanionMood; talkPulse?: number; size: number;
                     //   className?: string; onClick?: () => void; title?: string; greet?: boolean }
loadCompanionAssets(): Promise<CompanionAssets>       // manifest + all configs, fetched once and cached
randomLook(assets, rng?: () => number): CompanionLook  // weighted and compatibility-aware
renderCompanionImage(look, size, mood?): Promise<string> // off-screen PNG data URL (Dock icon, thumbnails)
```

The pure logic lives in `src/shared/companionLogic.ts` (compatibility checks including the hat rules, normalizing a look, weighted randomization, event scheduling) and is unit-tested.

**Behaviour:**
- **Loading:** GLTFLoader with `MeshoptDecoder`. Every file is fetched and parsed once per URL (a promise cache) and cloned per instance; geometries are shared.
- **Assembly:** load the rig, attach the head at `anchor:head`, then attach the other parts at the head's (or rig's) anchors, applying the `hat-config` adjustment for hats and headphones (the worn hair's replacement when there is one).
- **Look:** every mesh gets `MeshToonMaterial` with a 3-step gradient and the tint or paint colour, plus an inverted-hull outline in a darkened skin tone.
- **Face:** the `face` mesh gets a `CanvasTexture`. The compositor draws eyes (the variant), pupils (offset by gaze), brows and mouth from cached SVG images. It redraws only when the face state or gaze changes.
- **Animation:** an `AnimationMixer` loops the mood's clip (`MOOD_CLIP`) with 0.25 s crossfades. One-shots (`wave` when `greet` is set, `poke` on click) play once, then fall back to the mood clip.
- **Events:** `animation-events.json` cues fire as the clip time crosses them, including across loop wrap.
- **Face timing:** blinks come every 2.5–5 s at random, plus blink events. Talking alternates `talk-small` and `talk-wide` with talk energy.
- **Pointer:** gaze follows the pointer through pupils and a small extra rotation of `head-pivot`, applied after the mixer.
- **Framing:** views fit the whole character; live views under 80 px (the agent panel) frame head and shoulders instead, so the face stays readable. Stills (`renderCompanionImage`) show the clip's opening pose and apply its opening prop cue.
- **Performance:**
  - one renderer per canvas, with the pixel ratio capped at 2;
  - rendering pauses when off-screen or the window is hidden;
  - reduced motion slows clips and stops the bigger one-shots;
  - everything is disposed on unmount.
- **Fallback:** if WebGL or loading fails, draw the 2D face layers in a tinted circle. Never leave a blank box.
- **Test hook:** set `window.__atelierCompanionStats = { ready, errors }`; the smoke test asserts that instances rendered without errors, and that the editor shows its part chips, face swatches, palettes and a thumbnail for every preset.

## Bring your own designs

The engine draws whatever art it is given, so a fork (a build you distribute as your own product), or any build that won't use Atelier's characters, brings its own designs and changes no engine code. Everything it loads comes from one folder and one branding file:

| What | Where the engine loads it | Format |
|---|---|---|
| The manifest | `src/renderer/public/companion/manifest.json` | `CompanionManifest`: every rig, part, face layer and config file by path, with labels |
| Rigs | `rigs/<A\|B\|C>.glb` | glTF binary (meshopt allowed) with the node hierarchy, `RIG_NODES` and one animation per `CLIPS` name; see [3D conventions](#3d-conventions) |
| Parts | `parts/<part-id>.glb` | one root node named by the id; heads carry the `face` mesh and the `anchor:*` nodes; materials `tint:<skin\|hair\|accent\|outfit>` and `paint:<name>` |
| Face layers | `face/<face-id>/<variant>.svg`, and `pupils.svg` for eyes | 512×256 transparent SVGs, one per variant; see [Face layer conventions](#face-layer-conventions) |
| Rules and presets | `config/*.json` | head and hat compatibility, hat seats, pupil ranges, randomization palettes, animation events and `presets.json` (`CompanionPreset[]`) |
| The default companion | `branding/<id>/companion.json` (named by `branding.json`'s `companion` and `defaultPreset`) | one `CompanionPreset`: name, tagline, personality, summary and a look of part ids, face ids and colours |

The renderer fetches the folder from `app://atelier/companion/` (Vite copies `src/renderer/public/` into the build), main reads `config/presets.json` and the compatibility rules from the same folder (the source folder in a dev run, `out/renderer/companion/` when built), and the kit copies it to `/__atelier/kit/1/companion/` for apps. Looks, `.ateliercompanion` files and a cast member's `look` hold only ids and colours, never geometry, so they draw with whichever art the build has.

To swap in your own:

1. Replace the files in `src/renderer/public/companion/` with your own, made by a generator of your own or exported from a 3D tool, in the formats above. Keep the slot, anchor, clip and tint names; to use other part or face ids, change `PART_IDS`, `FACE_IDS` and the variant lists in `src/shared/companion.ts` (MPL) to match your manifest.
2. Replace `scripts/companion-assets/` with your generator, or remove it and the `companion:assets` script, so nothing writes Atelier's art back.
3. Write your own `config/presets.json` (or `[]`), and give your branding a `companion.json` with a look from your parts; set `hiddenPresets` to the presets you leave out.
4. Draw your own icons (`branding/unofficial/icon.svg` and `scripts/app-icons/unofficial.mjs`), and leave `branding/official/` out of your builds.
5. Run `npx vitest run tests/companionAssets.test.ts tests/brandingSwitch.test.ts`: they check the folder against the contract (every file referenced and present, every variant, the triangle budgets, presets with valid looks) and the branding's default companion. Change their checks of Atelier's own presets (six, Pip first) to yours.

## Integration (main and chrome)

- **Profile:** a companion is a `CompanionProfile` from `src/shared/companion.ts`: its name, look, personality and settings.
  - `CompanionStore` migrates older profiles and sanitizes ids against `PART_IDS` and `FACE_IDS`, colours (`#rrggbb`), name length and persona.
  - The service methods are `companion.get`, `companion.set(patch)`, `companion.presets()` (the branding's own companion first, then the generated `presets.json`'s that the branding offers) and `companion.setDockIcon(pngDataUrl)`.
- **Persona:** the preset's `personality` is added to the system prompt when a chat starts and stays in that chat's snapshot.
- **Settings › Companions** lists every companion (hidden ones too), each opening its card, with create, import and, on macOS, the Dock icon toggle.
- **The companion card** (`atelier://companion/<id>`, `src/renderer/src/companion-card/`) edits a companion, and its look is edited in place on the card:
  - the figure stays centred, with one toolbar for undo, redo and four shuffle styles;
  - a ring of bubbles around it, one per category (shape: the body, head and ears; eyes, mouth and brows; hair, hat, accessories and colours), each opening an option card;
  - the colours card offers the palettes from `randomization-config` and a free colour picker;
  - parts a head does not accept are disabled. A hat can still be picked over hair or ears it does not go with and replaces them; picking such hair or ears afterwards takes the hat off (the latest pick wins);
  - every change saves as it is made.
- **New companions:** the new-companion sheet offers a shuffled companion and the presets; an `.ateliercompanion` file is reviewed before it is added.
- **Welcome:** the welcome flow offers a shuffled companion, the presets and naming.
- **Accent colour:** the chrome's accent colour follows `look.colors.accent`.
- **Dock icon (macOS):** when enabled, the chrome renders the companion off-screen at 512 px and main calls `app.dock.setIcon`.
- **CSP:** the UI's CSP allows `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` so the meshopt decoder can compile WebAssembly, and nothing more.
